Record Q3 - total sales $94.9M (+158%), domestic +214% to $84.5M, beating the prior Q2 record by 46% sequentially.
GAAP gross margin fell to 40% from 47.6%; management argued ~7.5% of the decline was one-time / short-term, implying a normalized ~47.2% margin.
Net income declined to $2.7M ($0.04 EPS) from $4.8M ($0.06) despite the revenue surge, pressured by margin compression and a 174% S&M jump.
Management framed the margin pressure as a deliberate 'cautious decision' to build operational infrastructure ahead of revenue.
Two new 2022 US can contracts will move Celsius away from spot-rate and international cans, materially reducing can costs vs 2021.
Six-orbit warehouse build (two to six warehouses) raises near-term costs; expected to turn into a freight/stock-out tailwind in 2022.
Industry-wide aluminum can shortage and port congestion stranded international cans, forcing expensive spot purchases as aluminum prices rose.
Industry freight cost up ~20% YoY per DAT Trendlines.
$104M nine-month inventory build drove a $52M operating cash outflow; management said cash flow would be +$50M+ ex-inventory build, ~$13M fully normalized; ~$40M prepaids should normalize.
Fitness/vending rebounded to triple-digit growth, contributing ~$5.2M incremental revenue.
Coke Energy discontinuation allowed incremental distribution capture outside normal reset windows; larger resets expected March-April 2022.
Celsius is one of the 'lone outliers' not yet taking price; evaluating pricing and promotional architecture; competitors are pulling back promotions.
New global uniform can design launched in September; Sweden share dipped early in Q3 on the redesign, recovering to 9.3% by September.
FAST bar launched in the US (Amazon, +50% sequentially) and on Amazon EU; new Finnish RTD protein line launched Q4 (300,000 initial orders, higher margin).
Costco became a 10%+ revenue customer with Costco.com rollout; Sam's Club launching in Q4 test markets.
Management declined to give forward leverage guidance and was non-committal on the exact timing of margin normalization (pointed to back end of 2022).
Clarify whether Celsius intends to take price or is holding due to competition; does it look like competitors are reducing promotion or taking price in a way that would let Celsius follow?

Celsius is evaluating pricing, watching the top two players, and deploying promotional and pricing-architecture strategies. One-time charges (importing cans, freight) plus the six-orbit move would allow a return to normalized gross profit once international cans cycle through and spot purchases end; still evaluating which cost increases are permanent vs transitory. Confirmed competitors are pulling back promotions - 'we're not the anomaly.'
Growth Decomposition, DSD Conversion & Margin Vision
Kaumil Gajrawala, Credit Suisse / Kevin Grundy, Jefferies

Rough split of growth between new distribution and same-store sales; confirm DSD conversion (~50%, ~80% goal) and pace; longer-term margin vision; ability to fund the business organically given negative cash flow.

Coke Energy discontinuation drove incremental distribution captured outside reset windows; same-store sales rising via DSD migration. ~50% of MULO stores converted, ~80% the ideal goal, velocities meeting internal expectations, positive NACS show pointing to 2022 shelf-space gains. Margin path back to pre-COVID mid-to-upper-40s with scale upside. Business generates sufficient cash - $50M+ ex-inventory build, ~$13M fully normalized; ~$40M prepaids should normalize.
Six-Orbit Warehouse Cost Ramp & European Expansion; FAST/Protein Rollout
Extraordinary costs from the six-orbit warehouse strategy in Q4 / early 2022 and the P&L leverage contribution in 2022; plans for Germany/UK; rollout of FAST bars and the protein line.

Declined forward leverage guidance; warehouse costs rise into Q4 and beyond as Celsius invests ahead of revenue (two to six warehouses). UK/Germany serviced via Amazon, in talks with larger distributors; international uses an asset-light model invoicing in USD to avoid FX exposure. FAST: additional bar orders placed, US manufacturing planned for 2022; new Finnish RTD protein line carries a higher margin profile.
FAST/Protein SKU Counts, US Manufacturing, Coolers & Vibe Flavors
Number of FAST and protein-line SKUs in the US; whether US manufacturing is anticipated in 2022; cooler aspirations for Q4 and 2022; updates on US Vibe-line flavors/SKUs.

FAST has two flavors on Amazon (more under evaluation given import challenges); the Finnish RTD protein line comes in three flavors. US manufacturing of FAST bars anticipated in 2022. 900+ coolers placed in 9M (400 in Q3) with a methodical approach. Vibe line (Peach, Tropical) a top seller; a new undisclosed Vibe coming 'this summer.'
Door Count, DSD Partner Count & Freight Strategy

Confirm the 118,000 door count and how many added in the quarter; confirm 224 regional DSD partners covering 92% of US counties; how Celsius plans to deal with the industry-wide freight issue through year-end and 2022.

Confirmed 118,000 storefronts (~40% YTD increase) with significant further new-door opportunity, especially convenience via DSD. Confirmed 224 regional DSD partners covering ~92% of US counties - the largest quarterly partner increase. On freight, moving from two to six warehouses currently means costly LTL shipping; the six-orbit model will let distributors take full truckloads over shorter distances, generating synergistic freight benefits at scale.

What is 'normalized' gross margin going forward (pre-COVID or beyond, ex-freight)? Should the margin 'puts and takes' be read as percentage points? To what extent is the inventory build a logistical buffer versus feeding demand?

Margins include freight; expects a return to ~46-47% (2020 levels) with upside at scale - characterized as mid-to-upper 40s, framed as a timing issue (full benefits perhaps by the back end of 2022). Confirmed the cost callouts are percentage points off gross margin (~3% can/input plus freight, summing to ~7%). The Q3 inventory build was to fulfill demand and stock the six new warehouses; forward-looking inventory is ~120 days, within the optimal range.
